frequency_question: How often do bilateral transboundary water treaties in South Asia successfully secure a formal signed extension or replacement prior to or immediately upon expiration?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral water-sharing treaties involving India and a coterminous neighbor that reached a 30-year or similar long-term structural milestone requiring renegotiation. Excludes informal advisory committees or non-treaty memoranda of understanding.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Implementation and Continuous Operation

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; universe of exact 30-year treaty renewals involving India is extremely small, rendering this the exhaustive population of direct analogues.
known_gaps: Extremely small sample size due to the unique 30-year lifespan of major treaties in the region.
skeleton: Named instances of major bilateral water pacts or milestone renewals involving South Asian riparians where structural continuity was tested.
multiplier: 3 historical episodes examined for structural analogues to long-term water pact renewals.
validity_reason: The geopolitical baseline for South Asian bilateral river negotiations remains stable until significant structural shifts occur in regional multilateral frameworks.
